summary.headline: Timex Group India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% to INR359 crore and EBITDA 54% to INR66 crore, a record quarter, with product margin down 1.1pp.
summary.overview: Management reported its largest quarter in company history, with revenue of about INR359 crore (up 47% YoY), EBITDA of about INR66 crore (up 54%) and PBT of about INR64 crore (up 57%). E-commerce grew 75% to about INR190 crore, while trade grew 34% to about INR85 crore. Product gross margin fell about 1.1pp YoY on raw material inflation (copper, gold, silver), movement costs and a weaker rupee (USD near INR97 at peak), partly offset by an April price increase of 5-15% on selected SKUs. Management guided to a 20% EBITDA margin over the long term, without giving formal revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR100 crore cited for WIP and components, INR40-45 crore consignment

segments.name: Timex brand
segments.commentary: Grew 67% in Q2, faster than company. Own brands about 60% of revenue (up from about 55% a year ago). Marketing spend kept at 10-11% of Timex revenue.

segments.name: GUESS
segments.commentary: Grew 57% in Q2. Trailing 12-month company-realised sales about INR175 crore, with retail value about INR500 crore per management.

segments.name: Licensed portfolio and OEM
segments.commentary: Licensed portfolio about 25% of revenue and OEM about 15%, per management, both down from earlier mix as own brands gained share.

segments.name: Exclusive retail
segments.commentary: Grew 48% in Q2; about 4 stores added in the quarter, 44 stores now, all franchise-owned and operated. Plan of 200+ stores over 3 years.

segments.name: E-commerce sub-channels
segments.commentary: 1P is the largest; marketplace (3P) growing about 300%; quick commerce live on six platforms; dot-coms (timex.com, helix.com, justwatches.com).

segments.name: Aston Martin
segments.commentary: Launched November 2025; added about 14 doors in the quarter, taking total to 100 points of sale.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal revenue guidance; it says the growth achieved in the last five years is doable again.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of about 20%, reached over a year or so; management prioritises rupee EBITDA over margin percentage.
Q3 expected to be bigger than in prior years, with inventory built for Diwali and Valentine's sell-in. Management says Q3 will still be smaller than Q2.
Product margin pressure expected to ease in Q3 as gold, silver and copper prices fell, though the dollar is still around INR95-96.
TMX (entry price sub-brand, about INR700 entry point) to be scaled 2-3x from 2027 onwards.
Plans to open about 40 stores in 2027, 80-100 in 2028 and 70-80 in 2029.
Guess top sellers to be assembled in India from April 2027 (Q1 FY28).
Plan to add an entry-level Swiss brand; details expected in 3-4 months.
capex_capacity: Baddi single-shift capacity is 6 million units per year; utilisation is at almost 100%. The factory ran double shift for a few months this quarter.
A second building of equal size is planned by about May 2027, taking physical capacity to 12 million; capex about USD1.2 million.
Assembly lines are added in about 45 days versus about 6 months for buildings. Plan is 6 to 8 million units in FY28 and 12 million in 2-3 years.
Q2 volume about 2.5 million watches, of which Timex is about 64-65% by volume.
Exploring a partnership with a movement manufacturer for Timex movements, at an early stage.
demand_pricing: Average price increase of about 8-8.5% from April 2026 across brands, applied to selected SKUs, ranging 5-15%.
Revenue growth split roughly 50% volume and 50% value (ASP and mix) in Q2 and H1.
Management says the analog watch category is growing about 14-15% versus 8-9% historically.
Competition in the INR2,000-10,000 band is a duopoly with Titan; Timex is about one-quarter of Titan's scale in that brand, per management.
Products above INR10,000 are about 14% of business, with a Timex product up to INR30,000 and Guess automatics at about INR30,000.
Duties on imports about 22%; making in India saves about 10-12% of material cost.
Marketing about 8-8.5% of company revenue, and 10-11% of Timex revenue.
Costume jewellery (Guess, sold as distributor) is immaterial; Timex jewellery is planned for the future.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of Q2 revenue growth between volume and price/mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is roughly 50-50 between volume and value (ASP and mix) for both Q2 and H1.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is achievable, and what is the Q3 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees about 20% EBITDA as achievable over time, with H1 at 17.5%; it prioritises rupee EBITDA and top-line share over margin percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and what is the DSO?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on the large quarter's sell-in; DSO is 19 days, the lowest ever on a 12-month rolling basis, against credit terms of 30-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: What drove gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation (movements, copper, gold, silver) and a weaker rupee (USD near INR97) cut product gross margin by about 1.1pp YoY, partly offset by price increases.

qa_highlights.question: How many stores in 2027 and how fast will TMX grow?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 stores in 2027, 80-100 in 2028 and 70-80 in 2029; TMX to grow 2-3x starting 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Are there capital needs or promoter sales?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is asset-light with franchise stores and no major consignment capital. The factory is fully depreciated and no near-term borrowing is needed. The promoter holds 51%.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from the rupee (USD around INR95-97) and imported movement and component costs from Japan and China.
Dependence on Flipkart, Amazon and Myntra for e-commerce; any multi-brand FDI rule change could hit the 1P channel.
Inventory at INR358 crore and receivables up sharply; watch whether Q3 sales meet the build-up.
Movement supply tightness globally; Baddi capacity at 100% utilisation.
Competition from global brands above INR15,000 and Titan's response.
Whether the 20% EBITDA margin is reached, given the current 17.5% H1 and the cost pressures.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, brand and channel strategy. Notably cautious on margins and forex, and it repeatedly declined to give numerical guidance on revenue, citing company policy.

We are more concerned about rupee EBITDA rather than percentage EBITDA.
Baddi has been utilized at 100% almost, and about six, seven months back we expanded the capacity to six million.

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management says five-year growth is repeatable and Q3 will be bigger than prior years, backed by Baddi capacity doubling from 6m to 12m (second building ~May 2027, capex ~USD1.2m) at 100% utilisation, plus store and TMX/Guess expansion plans, with ~20% long-term EBITDA margin target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 17.5% vs 14.5% in FY26 and management targets about 20% in a year or so, but product gross margin fell about 1.1pp YoY on copper, gold, silver and a USD near INR97, with Q3 pressure only expected to ease.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Second Baddi building of equal size is under construction to take capacity from 6m to 12m units/yr, with utilisation at almost 100% and a double shift run for a few months this quarter.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue growth is about 50% volume and 50% value in Q2 and H1, Q3 is expected to be bigger than prior years, and analog watch category is growing 14-15% vs 8-9% historically.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is at almost 100% and the Baddi building is the only major capacity step; a 6-8m unit assembly-line expansion for FY28 and 12m in 2-3 years is planned, which implies further capex announcements.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal revenue guidance; management says five-year growth pace is repeatable and Q2 revenue rose 47% with E-commerce up 75%, but cites margin and forex headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on margins and forex, and the 20% EBITDA target depends on reaching it from 17.5% H1 while USD is around INR95-97 and inventory is INR358 crore against receivables up to INR120 crore from INR58 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Entry-level Swiss brand details expected in 3-4 months, TMX to be scaled 2-3x from 2027, and Guess top sellers to be assembled in India from April 2027.

rows.label: Exclusive retail store rollout (about 40 stores in 2027, 200+ over 3 years)
rows.why: 44 stores now after about 4 added in Q2, with plan of about 40 in 2027, 80-100 in 2028 and 70-80 in 2029 across franchise formats.

rows.label: Price increases of 5-15% on selected SKUs
rows.why: Average price increase about 8-8.5% applied from April 2026 offset part of the 1.1pp product margin drop and drives about half of revenue growth.

rows.label: India assembly of Guess top sellers and in-house movement sourcing
rows.why: Guess top sellers move to India assembly from April 2027, where making in India saves about 10-12% of material cost against about 22% import duties; movement partnership is at an early stage.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, Baddi capacity doubling, store roll-out and TMX scaling, but cautious on gross margin, rupee and inventory build; analysts pushed on volume vs price split, the 20% margin path, receivables and DSO.
